study: Wiggins/Sawtell/Jerrim 2017, Learner Response System (handheld classroom-feedback devices) teacher PD, EEF eval (UCL IoE)
eval_evidence: EEF-funded trial 'independently evaluated by a team from the Institute of Education at University' (UCL IoE); the intervention was developed by a separate party (Edge Hill University).
developer_evidence: The Edge Hill University project team (which devised the LRS intervention) trained teachers to deliver it; 'A team from Edge Hill University developed the intervention and trained teachers to deliver it to pupils.'
cascade_evidence: The Edge Hill project team (project lead and Head of Training and Support) ran the training events directly for the participating teachers; no train-the-trainer / lead-teacher hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control condition was 'business as usual' within schools; control schools received no LRS training or devices.
coaching_evidence: PD was an initial 2-day introductory training event plus five half-termly one-day training sessions and web-based resource sharing; no ongoing in-class coaching/observation cycles of teachers in their own classrooms.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes teacher practice via handheld classroom-feedback devices used within normal lessons; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or independent student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Program newly rolled out into all schools simultaneously; outcomes include an end-of-Year-1 cohort (Cohort A, teachers new to LRS) and an end-of-Year-2 cohort (Cohort B). First measurement wave is the first implementation year, so coded first_year (note: a 2-year-dose cohort also exists).
